title: Power Automate: bring your own connection in attended and unattended cloud-triggered desktop flow runs
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned cloud-run capability from today's documented embedding requirements. The maker control, ownership restrictions and data-policy behaviour are supported; searches found no published feature-specific switch, default or licensing terms. All four Learn pages flagged by the pre-check opened successfully.

claims.claim: The roadmap item concerns Power Automate.
claims.quote: "products": ["Power Automate"]

claims.claim: Microsoft plans bring your own connections for shared desktop flows containing connector operations in attended and unattended cloud-triggered runs.
claims.quote: This functionality allows you to bring your own connections in shared desktop flows that include connector operations and need to run in attended or unattended mode, eliminating the need for embedded connection references in cloud runs.

claims.quote: Select the desktop flow in Power Automate (make.powerautomate.com), and then select **Details**. ... In the **Connection references** section, select **Manage**. ... Set the **Embedded in desktop flow** option to **Yes** to enable it.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Embedding or removing a reference requires ownership of the underlying connection.
claims.quote: You can only embed or remove connection references from a desktop flow if you own the underlying connection.

claims.claim: Other co-owners can manage only the connection references they added.
claims.quote: Other co-owners can only manage connection references they add.

claims.claim: Embedded connection references are available to other co-owners only within the respective shared desktop flow.
claims.quote: Embedded connection references are only available to other co-owners in the scope of the shared desktop flow.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Embedding gives other co-owners access to the underlying connection's data for modifying and running the flow.
claims.quote: By embedding a connection reference to a desktop flow, you allow other co-owners to have access to the underlying data provided by it, for both modifying as well as running the desktop flow.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Today's documented cloud invocation of desktop flows containing connector actions requires the Power Automate v2 schema.
claims.quote: To successfully invoke a desktop flow containing connector actions from a cloud flow, it must meet the following two requirements: ... The desktop flow must use the Power Automate v2 schema.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; controls[0]
claims.claim: For co-owners, today's cloud-initiated runs require all connection references to be embedded.
claims.quote: If you're a co-owner of the flow, all of its connection references must be marked as embedded.

claims.claim: Run-only users can currently run these shared flows only through attended desktop-console runs.
claims.quote: Makers with user access on a shared desktop flow must always bring their own connections when they run the flow. They can only perform attended console initiated runs.

claims.claim: Run-only users must supply their own connections when running the shared flow.
claims.quote: Makers with user access on a shared desktop flow must always bring their own connections when they run the flow.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Each connection is specific to a user.
claims.quote: Each connection is specific to a user and requires authentication to ensure secure access to data and services.

claims.claim: Connections require authentication, typically OAuth, API keys or another service-provided method.
claims.quote: This authentication is typically done using OAuth, API keys, or other authentication methods provided by the external service.

claims.claim: Sharing a desktop flow does not automatically give access to its underlying connections.
claims.quote: Sharing a desktop flow does not automatically provide access to the underlying connections utilized.

claims.claim: Connector actions can access and act on data reachable through the underlying authenticated connection.
claims.quote: This connection allows Power Automate to access and perform actions on data from various services, such as Microsoft 365, SharePoint, SQL Server, and many others.

claims.claim: Connector actions use a connection, represented by a connection reference, to act under its authenticated identity.
claims.quote: In Power Automate, a connection reference is an abstraction layer that points to a specific connection used by actions within your flows.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described which user's connector connection the planned cloud-run BYOC capability selects or who chooses it.
claims.quote: Searched: "bring your own connection" "cloud" "connector" "unattended" account credentials; opened cloudconnectors and sharing. Their selection and prompt descriptions cover console runs, not planned cloud-run BYOC.

claims.claim: Storage of a supplied connection under the planned unattended cloud-run BYOC capability is not described.
claims.quote: Searched: "bring your own connection" "cloud" "connector" "unattended" account credentials; opened cloudconnectors, sharing and use-connector-actions. None describes connection storage for planned cloud-run BYOC.

claims.claim: Prompting for a supplied connection during planned unattended cloud-run BYOC is not described.
claims.quote: Searched: "bring your own connection" "cloud" "connector" "unattended" account credentials; opened cloudconnectors and sharing. The documented BYOC prompt and suppression conditions are for console-initiated runs.

claims.claim: Importing a solution containing a desktop flow with embedded connection references does not automatically include the required references.
claims.quote: When importing a desktop flow with embedded connection references in a solution, the required connection references aren't automatically included.

claims.claim: The documented workaround is to explicitly include the required references in the solution alongside the desktop flow.
claims.quote: To work around this current limitation, explicitly include the required connection references in the solution alongside the desktop flow.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether planned cloud-run BYOC changes this solution-import limitation.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/desktop-flows bring your own connection cloud initiated runs embedded connection references; opened sharing and cloudconnectors; read roadmap. None addresses the future capability's solution-import behaviour.

claims.claim: Whether the v2 schema prerequisite remains for the planned cloud-run BYOC feature is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "bring your own connection" "cloud" "unattended" "schema"; opened cloudconnectors and sharing; read roadmap. Current v2 requirements are documented, but no text addresses their future status for cloud-run BYOC.

claims.claim: Default desktop-flow cloud connectors include Microsoft Dataverse, SharePoint, Office 365 Outlook and Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: Power Automate for desktop adds these cloud connectors to desktop flows by default. You always see them in the actions pane: ... Microsoft Dataverse ... SharePoint ... Microsoft Teams ... Office 365 Outlook

claims.claim: Other non-custom Power Automate cloud connectors can be added to desktop flows through the Assets library.
claims.quote: To add other non-custom Power Automate cloud connectors to a desktop flow, use the Assets library.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified the connector coverage of the planned cloud-run BYOC capability.
claims.quote: Searched: "bring your own connection" "cloud" "connector" "unattended" account credentials; opened cloudconnectors and use-connector-actions; read roadmap. General connector availability is described, but no feature-specific coverage list was found.

claims.claim: No source states an automatic change to existing flows on arrival, rather than the availability of the planned alternative to embedding.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Automate" "bring your own connection" "cloud" "default"; opened cloudconnectors and sharing; read roadmap. The record plans removal of the need to embed but says nothing about automatic migration or changed defaults for existing flows.

claims.claim: Embedding is a current per-reference setting on the selected shared desktop flow, not a documented switch for the future BYOC capability.
claims.quote: In the Connection references screen, view all of the connection references used in the flow. ... Set the Embedded in desktop flow option to Yes to enable it. ... After you confirm your selection, the connection reference is embedded in the desktop flow.

claims.claim: Existing desktop-flow data policies classify action groups as business or non-business.
claims.quote: Power Automate offers administrators the option to create and enforce policies that classify desktop flows action groups as business or non-business and mark actions or action groups as blocked.

claims.claim: Existing desktop-flow data policies can block actions or action groups.
claims.quote: Apart from marking action groups as business and non-business, the administrator can mark action groups or particular actions as blocked. In this case, these actions can't be used at all in the flow.

claims.claim: A desktop flow suspended for a data-policy violation cannot run.
claims.quote: A desktop flow that violates a data loss prevention (DLP) policy will be marked as suspended and the run option will be disabled.

claims.claim: A cloud flow using a suspended desktop flow cannot run it.
claims.quote: For cases that a desktop flow is suspended, it won't be able to run it. Similarly, a cloud flow using a suspend desktop flow won't be able to run either.

claims.claim: No incremental feature-specific meter or price was found, leaving review time as the identified incremental cost rather than asserting free licensing.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate bring your own connection attended unattended cloud triggered runs licensing premium Process license; read cloudconnectors, licensing/types and licensing FAQ excerpts. General RPA costs are published; no additional BYOC-specific charge was found.
